# Methods: Viral family composition (reads-based)
### Inputs
`PASS CSV` (r0366, combined PCR reps):
`…/fullacc/250828-r0366-X-PCRreps.COMBINED.PASS.recalc.csv`

`PASS CSV` (r0368):
`…/fullacc/250904-r0368-X-01-A3405_filtered.simple.abs50.bgx4.PASS.csv`

Each PASS CSV contains at least these columns: *accession,family,genus,total_MQ30,….*

### Preprocessing (r0366 set of 3 PCR replicates)
  - Merge PASS CSVs from the three r0366 PCR replicates (technical replicates, same library): mergePASScsv.py 
  - aggregates by accession:
    - total_MQ30 → sum across replicates
    - family/genus → first non-empty (should agree)
    - peak positions → union (dedup)
    - background stats → weighted averages / totals (see script header)
  - Recompute peak heights from the summed bedGraph (faithful to the combined signal):
  - `mergePeakcalc.py` fills the peak_heights column by looking up each peak_positions site in the combined bedGraph.
Output: `250828-r0366-X-PCRreps.COMBINED.PASS.recalc.csv` (now behaves like a per-sample PASS CSV)


### Family fractions CSV (reads-based)
  - summarize each PASS CSV (in this case, 2) into a long-format table with one row per (sample, family):
  - value = sum of total_MQ30 reads for all accessions in that family (within the sample)
    - fraction = value / sum(value) within that sample (so fractions per sample sum to 1.0)

  - Run this for the two samples, r0366_combined and r0368, then row-bind into:
    - family_fractions.ALL.csv with columns: sample,family,value,fraction.
    - Row-binding just stacks the two per-sample tables; doesn't average or sum across samples. Each bar is already 100% normalized within its own sample.
    
  
```{r}
# ---------- Setup ----------
# One-time installs 
# install.packages(c("tidyverse","scales","viridis"))

library(tidyverse)  # ggplot2, readr, dplyr, etc.
library(scales)     # percent_format
library(viridis)    # colorblind-safe palettes
```


```{r}
# Location of the combined long CSV (copied locally after familyFractions.py script)
fullacc_dir <- "/Users/jeaninegezelle/Desktop/viromelib/fullacc"
ff <- readr::read_csv(file.path(fullacc_dir, "family_fractions.ALL.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)

# Fix sample order on the x-axis (left→right)
ff$sample <- factor(ff$sample, levels = c("r0366_combined","r0368"))
```


```{r}
# ---------- Legend: show overall share across BOTH samples ----------
# Legend *“overall share”* is read-weighted across samples (sum of value per family divided by total value across both samples).
# Sum over samples to get a global share per family; use it to
# (1) order legend families and (2) add "(12.3%)" style labels.
legend_totals <- ff %>%
  group_by(family) %>%
  summarise(overall = sum(value), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(overall_frac = overall / sum(overall))

families <- legend_totals %>% arrange(desc(overall_frac)) %>% pull(family)

legend_labels <- setNames(
  paste0(
    families, " (",
    percent(legend_totals$overall_frac[match(families, legend_totals$family)], accuracy = 0.1),
    ")"
  ),
  families
)
```

### pick the color palette:
```{r}
# High-contrast, colorblind-safe palette: 

# pal <- setNames(viridis(length(families), option = "inferno"), families)
# or 
# pal <- setNames(scales::hue_pal(l=65, c = 100) (length(families)),families) # hue_pal instead, hue jumps instead of gradients 
# or
# pal <- setNames(viridis(length(families), option = "turbo"), families) # viridis but with turbo mode for contrast

# or
# for colors, highlight only the top families, keep others softer, but still diff colors
top_k <- 8
pal_top   <- setNames(scales::hue_pal(l=60,  c=100)(top_k), families[1:top_k])
pal_rest  <- setNames(scales::hue_pal(l=85, c=35)(length(families)-top_k), families[(top_k+1):length(families)])
pal <- c(pal_top, pal_rest)


# lock factor order for stacking & legend
ff$family <- factor(ff$family, levels = families)
```


```{r}
# ----------labels ----------
# Print % labels inside segments ≥3% so small slivers don’t get cluttered
label_df <- ff %>%
  mutate(lbl = if_else(fraction >= 0.03, percent(fraction, accuracy = 1), ""))
# Per-sample total reads (to print under each bar)
totals_df <- ff %>%
  group_by(sample) %>%
  summarise(total_reads = sum(value), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(label = paste0("n = ", scales::comma(total_reads)),
         y = -0.06)  # vertical offset below 0 (tweak if needed)

```


```{r}
# ---------- Plot ----------
p <- ggplot(ff, aes(x = sample, y = fraction, fill = family)) +
  # Bars: wider width & thin white edges for separation
  geom_col(width = 0.95, color = "white", linewidth = 0.3) +
  # In-bar % labels
  geom_text(
    data = label_df,
    aes(label = lbl),
    position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5),
    size = 3, color = "white", lineheight = 0.9
  ) +
  # y-axis as percent; tiny top padding so labels don't touch the frame
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent_format(accuracy = 1),
                     expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.03))) +
  # Custom legend: families ordered by global share, label shows "(xx.x%)"
  scale_fill_manual(values = pal, breaks = families, labels = legend_labels,
                    name = "Family (overall share)") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Fraction of total_MQ30") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    # Diagonal x labels for extra space
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, vjust = 1, margin = margin(t = 6)),
    plot.margin  = margin(t = 10, r = 12, b = 24, l = 12)
  )

print(p)
```


```{r}
# ---------- Save ----------
ggsave(file.path(fullacc_dir, "family_fractions_reads.pdf"), p, width = 8.5, height = 4.5)
ggsave(file.path(fullacc_dir, "family_fractions_reads.png"), p, width = 8.5, height = 4.5, dpi = 300)

```

## this block includes script to make the family fractions plot csv - *not used* - since already had .csv from python script$ROOT/scripts/familyFractions.py

```{r}
# If needed once: install.packages(c("tidyverse","scales","viridis"))
library(tidyverse)
library(scales)
library(viridis)

# ---- paths (edit if needed) ----
fullacc_dir <- "/Users/jeaninegezelle/Desktop/viromelib/fullacc"
pass_paths <- c(
  r0366_combined = file.path(fullacc_dir, "250828-r0366-X-PCRreps.COMBINED.PASS.recalc.csv"),
  r0368          = file.path(fullacc_dir, "250904-r0368-X-01-A3405_filtered.simple.abs50.bgx4.PASS.csv")
)
stopifnot(all(file.exists(pass_paths)))

# ---- helper: build long table by metric ----
make_family_df <- function(paths, metric = c("reads","count")) {
  metric <- match.arg(metric)
  purrr::imap_dfr(paths, function(pth, sample_label) {
    df <- readr::read_csv(pth, show_col_types = FALSE)
    df <- df %>% mutate(family = if_else(is.na(family) | family=="", "Unknown", family))
    if (metric == "reads") {
      if (!"total_MQ30" %in% names(df)) stop("PASS CSV lacks total_MQ30 for metric='reads'")
      out <- df %>%
        group_by(family) %>%
        summarise(value = sum(as.numeric(total_MQ30), na.rm = TRUE), .groups="drop")
    } else {
      out <- df %>%
        count(family, name = "value") %>%
        mutate(value = as.numeric(value))
    }
    out %>%
      mutate(sample = sample_label) %>%
      group_by(sample) %>%
      mutate(fraction = value / sum(value)) %>%
      ungroup()
  })
}

# ---- choose metric: "reads" (abundance) or "count" (accessions) ----
metric <- "reads"  # change to "count" if you prefer richness
ff <- make_family_df(pass_paths, metric = metric)

# ---- legend labels show overall share (across BOTH samples) ----
legend_totals <- ff %>%
  group_by(family) %>%
  summarise(overall = sum(value), .groups="drop") %>%
  mutate(overall_frac = overall / sum(overall))

families <- legend_totals %>% arrange(desc(overall_frac)) %>% pull(family)
legend_labels <- setNames(
  paste0(families, "  (", percent(legend_totals$overall_frac[match(families, legend_totals$family)], accuracy = 0.1), ")"),
  families
)

# consistent colors
pal <- setNames(viridis(length(families), option = "D"), families)

# order samples on x-axis
ff$sample <- factor(ff$sample, levels = names(pass_paths))
ff$family <- factor(ff$family, levels = families)

# (optional) inside-bar % labels per sample (hide very tiny slivers)
label_df <- ff %>%
  mutate(lbl = if_else(fraction >= 0.03, percent(fraction, accuracy = 1), ""))

p_family <- ggplot(ff, aes(x = sample, y = fraction, fill = family)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.8, color = "white", linewidth = 0.2) +
  geom_text(data = label_df, aes(label = lbl), position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5),
            size = 3, color = "white", lineheight = 0.9) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent_format(accuracy = 1), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, .02))) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = pal, breaks = families, labels = legend_labels, name = "Family (overall share)") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = ifelse(metric=="reads","Fraction of total_MQ30","Fraction of accessions")) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 12) +
  theme(panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
        legend.key.height = unit(0.5, "cm"),
        legend.title = element_text(size = 11),
        legend.text  = element_text(size = 10))

print(p_family)

# save
ggsave(file.path(fullacc_dir, paste0("family_fractions_", metric, ".pdf")), p_family, width = 7, height = 4)
ggsave(file.path(fullacc_dir, paste0("family_fractions_", metric, ".png")), p_family, width = 7, height = 4, dpi = 300)

```
